data.name: Instructions
data.value:
1. Connect your microphone or audio interface and install its audio driver. 2. Select its Windows input or ASIO driver in this tool. 3. Select the actual microphone channel; channel 1 is usually the first microphone input. 4. Select CABLE Input as the output. In Windows Sound, set CABLE Input and CABLE Output to 2 channels and 48 kHz if available. 5. Start the microphone. In FiveM voice settings, select CABLE Output. 6. Keep the tool running in the tray; stop to release the microphone.
For low latency, keep the extra buffer at 5 ms. In the VB-CABLE Control Panel, use matching 48 kHz sample rates and tune its own latency while FiveM and this tool are active. Follow the buffer statistics; a value that is too small causes dropouts. The extra buffer is only one part of the total latency.
For ASIO, match the sample rate in the interface driver. If the driver cannot serve multiple apps at once, use another output device for game audio.
If your voice is doubled in a Discord stream: stop, enable “Open CABLE exclusively (stream test)”, and start again. Allow exclusive access for CABLE Input in Windows Sound. Check that FiveM still receives the microphone and the second copy disappears from the stream. Clear the checkbox if this causes problems. The test does not prevent every type of capture.
This tool requires the existing VB-CABLE driver. It does not create a virtual recording device by itself.
